The provided solution correctly implements the divide-and-conquer algorithm to find the median, and the code will return the right answer. However, it fails to satisfy the **O(1) space complexity** constraint specified in the question. In Python, list slicing (`nums1[i:]`, `nums2[j:]`) creates new list copies, resulting in O(n) space usage, not O(1). Additionally, the recursion stack uses O(log n) space. The time complexity explanation is also inaccurate: while the slicing operations make the total runtime O(n), the algorithm itself is conceptually O(log n), and describing it as a "single pass" is misleading. To truly achieve O(1) space, the solution should use index pointers instead of slicing and be implemented iteratively (or the linear two-pointer merge approach should be used for O(n) time and O(1) space).

Rating: [[5]]
